transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

The 'DE' code on LG washer-dryers typically indicates a Door Error or that the door is not locked/unlocked correctly. This is often due to a safety delay rather than a hard fault. Many models keep the lock engaged for 1-2 minutes after a programme finishes to prevent burns from hot water or steam. Please leave the machine switched on and wait 5 minutes, then try opening the handle normally. If it remains locked, switch it off at the wall socket, wait another 5 minutes to reset the electronics, and try again. Let me know if the door opens after this.
its not locked tho, the door wont even lock, it just wont start. its got a king size duvet in if that matters

A single heavy item like a king-size duvet often causes an 'unbalanced load' fault on washer-dryers; the machine detects that the weight is stuck to one side and refuses to spin to prevent damage, which can look like a door or start error. Please redistribute the duvet evenly inside the drum, close the door firmly until it clicks, and try running just a drain/spin cycle. If it still fails to start or shows the DE code again after this, we will check if the door catch is obstructed or if there is an electrical fault with the lock.
ok tried closing it firmly, it closes but springs back a bit. still dE w the duvet in tho

The fact that the door 'springs back' when you close it suggests a mechanical issue with the latch rather than an electrical one. The door catch (the hook on the door) or the receiving slot may be broken, preventing the machine from sensing that the door is securely shut. Please switch off and unplug the machine for safety, then inspect the plastic hook on the door edge and the slot in the frame for any damage or obstructions.
ok unplugged it. hook looks fine, nothing broken. the duvet is bulging against the glass tho and a corner is squashed in the rubber seal

[Heading: Likely cause: overload / too full]
The 'springing back' combined with the duvet bulging against the glass suggests that the load is physically preventing the door from closing fully. The machine will not start because it cannot detect a secure seal, which triggers the DE error as a safety measure. To help us determine if this is purely an overload issue or if there is a secondary fault with the lock mechanism itself, I need to know exactly which model you have. Please check the sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door and tell me the full model number.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its FWV796WTSE, on the label. so is it just too much duvet in there?

[Heading: Likely cause: overload / too full]
Yes, the duvet is probably the root cause. A king-size duvet creates a massive, uneven load that can physically distort the door frame or snap the plastic catch hook inside when you try to force it shut. The 'springing back' and the squashed seal are classic signs of mechanical stress; even if the external hook looks fine, the internal latch may be broken or misaligned so the machine no longer detects a closed door. Because this involves opening the casing to inspect or replace the internal catch mechanism (which is behind the front panel), this is not an owner-safe repair. I recommend you remove the duvet and call an engineer to fit a new door catch assembly.
